test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: 3 years ago from now, the age of father was 30 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **age of son** 3 years ago be x.

**Father's age** then = 2x + 30.

Age difference = (2x + 30) − x = x + 30.

Difference in ages remains **constant** throughout life.

When father is twice the son's age, the difference (x + 30) must equal the **son's age** then.

Son's age then = x + 30. Current age of son = x + 3. Years from now = (x + 30) − (x + 3) = 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3 years ago, Father's age = 2 × Son's age + 30.

**Formula:** Age difference is constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e91d026f9f4b479b8f461f9bc3bbb468bd5776198ec33734a3df31ecc33645b.png] 

⇒ Let **Son's age** 3 years ago = S−₃ and **Father's age** = F−₃.

⇒ F−₃ = 2 × S−₃ + 30

⇒ **Age Difference** (D) = F−₃ − S−₃ = (2 × S−₃ + 30) − S−₃ = S−₃ + 30.

⇒ Let after **T years** from now, FT = 2 × ST.

⇒ Difference (D) = FT − ST = 2ST − ST = ST.

⇒ ST = S−₃ + 30.

⇒ Since ST is the age after T years from **present**, and S−₃ was age 3 years **before** present:

⇒ ST = Sₚᵣₑₛₑₙₜ + T = (S−₃ + 3) + T.

⇒ S−₃ + 30 = S−₃ + 3 + T.

⇒ T = 30 − 3 = 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains **constant** at any point in time.

Ratio of Ages

When the age of one person is **n times** the age of another, the age difference is equal to (n−1) × the younger person's age.

Time Displacement

If current age is x, then age **'a' years ago** is (x − a) and age **'b' years later** is (x + b).</p
